title: The next big asset class could come from emerging markets
gist: Ajay Banga and Dutch minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma pitch emerging-market private debt originated by MDBs/DFIs as a new institutional asset class: GEMs data show default rates comparable to developed markets, higher recoveries and low correlation; MDBs are standardizing how loans are packaged and transferred to pension funds to free balance sheets, targeting even 1% of USD 100 trillion institutional AUM (USD 1 trillion).

themes.theme: Jobs gap and the private capital imperative

insights.claim: Over the next 10 to 15 years 1.2 billion young people in developing countries will reach working age while their economies are expected to create only around 400 million jobs, an 800 million gap with implications for poverty, migration and stability.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: A massive jobs shortfall is a long-run driver of migration and political risk.
insights.quote: 1.2 billion young people in developing countries will reach working age, but their economies are expected to create only around 400 million jobs

insights.claim: The World Bank Group grew private capital mobilization from $35 billion in 2022 to $112 billion last year, compared with about $600 billion mobilized by all OECD countries between 2012 and 2024.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: MDB mobilization is scaling fast and becoming a meaningful channel for EM deal flow.
insights.quote: the World Bank Group has grown private capital mobilization from $35 billion in 2022 to $112 billion last year
insights.locator: We can therefore build on progress

insights.claim: Individual deal-by-deal mobilization only goes so far; the next frontier is bringing institutional capital into development at scale, as investing in emerging and frontier market businesses remains largely untapped.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Points to an emerging pipeline of MDB-sourced EM credit products for institutions.
insights.locator: Most of this has been done

themes.theme: MDB asset transfers to institutional investors

insights.claim: Multilateral development banks are shifting from holding business and infrastructure loans on their balance sheets to making them available to institutional investors, freeing capital for new projects.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Expect MDB loan sales, securitizations or participations as new EM private credit supply.
insights.quote: rather than keeping those assets, development banks are making them available to institutional investors

insights.claim: Pension funds need scale, diversification, reliable information and familiar structures and cannot assess thousands of individual loans, so the World Bank Group and five other MDBs are developing common ways to assess, document, package and transfer investments.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Standardized packaging is the key unlock; watch for pooled MDB-originated vehicles.
insights.quote: the World Bank Group and five other multilateral development banks are working on common ways to assess, document, package and transfer investments

insights.claim: ILX invests capital on behalf of Dutch and Danish pension funds alongside the IFC in sustainable forestry in Uruguay.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Concrete precedent of Nordic/Dutch pension capital co-investing with IFC.
insights.locator: The Netherlands and the World Bank

insights.claim: The Netherlands and the World Bank are partnering, combining the Bank's investments, country knowledge and risk management with Dutch financial expertise and institutional investors.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Dutch pensions likely early adopters of MDB-sourced EM credit.
insights.locator: The Netherlands and the World Bank

insights.claim: The Global Emerging Markets Risk Database (GEMs), with 30 years of MDB and DFI private loan data, shows average default rates on EM private debt comparable to developed markets and recovery rates above many global benchmarks.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Challenges the market's EM risk premium; MDB-originated EM private credit may be mispriced relative to realized losses.
insights.quote: the average default rate of EM market private debt is comparable to developed markets
insights.locator: The Global Emerging Markets Risk Database

insights.claim: Default patterns in MDB/DFI-originated EM private debt are only weakly correlated with developed markets, making it a compelling diversifier for institutional portfolios.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Portfolio construction argument for allocating to EM private credit via MDB channels.
insights.quote: the default patterns are only weakly correlated with developed markets
insights.locator: The Global Emerging Markets Risk Database

insights.claim: If only 1% of the USD 100 trillion of global institutional and pension fund AUM went to emerging and frontier markets, it would mean USD 1 trillion of extra investment in clean water, energy transition, healthcare and jobs.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Sizing of potential flows into EM infrastructure/credit if the asset class matures.
insights.quote: If only 1% of the USD 100 trillion assets under management
insights.locator: The World Bank Group has demonstrated
